collection_summary: Anchored-fuzzy causal instance for the `causal` query category. The natural-language query 'which countries are currently classified as politically fragile or unstable' has no objectively crisp answer because 'fragile or unstable' is a fuzzy political-classification concept; this instance anchors the inclusion criterion to the Fragile States Index (FSI), specifically all countries with FSI 2024 score ≥ 90 (Alert + High Alert + Very High Alert sub-tiers). 29 countries qualify across 4 continents. The LLM under test is measured on whether its parametric notion of 'politically fragile or unstable countries' agrees with the FSI 2024 Alert-tier list without being told FSI is the anchor (the table_title does not name FSI). Multi-attribute output (FSI Tier + FSI Score) exercises calibration: country membership = strong for obvious cases (Yemen, Syria, Somalia), weaker at boundary cases (Lebanon, Pakistan, Uganda); FSI tier = stable categorical given the score; FSI score = numeric anchor. Sources: 3 anchor articles (FSI master + List of countries by FSI for the data + continent-assignment article). Result: 29 rows × 4 columns, sorted by continent then country.
source_coverage_notes: Anchor articles (3): Wikipedia 'Fragile States Index' (defines the FSI tier system: Very High Alert ≥110, High Alert 100-109.9, Alert 90-99.9, Warning, Stable, Sustainable); 'List of countries by Fragile States Index' (data source for per-country 2024 scores and tier classifications — the article's most-recent year is 2024); 'List of sovereign states and dependent territories by continent' (source for continent partition assignments, UN M49-aligned). The 29 rows comprise all FSI 2024 Alert+ countries (score ≥ 90). The full FSI universe is ~178 scored countries; the 149 not in this CSV have FSI 2024 < 90 (Warning, Stable, or Sustainable tiers) and are excluded by the criterion. The next country below the threshold is Venezuela at 89.0. Continent coverage is sparse for South America (0 rows — no SA country has FSI 2024 ≥ 90; Venezuela is the closest at 89.0), Oceania (0 rows), Antarctica (0 rows). The protocol §4 Tier C example for `causal` mentions 'Alert' and 'High Alert' tiers; this instance includes the third Alert sub-tier 'Very High Alert' (≥ 110) — which is logically MORE unstable, not less — under the assumption that the protocol's two-tier nomenclature reflects older FSI labeling. Including all three Alert sub-tiers is the principled choice; if the auditor prefers strictly 'Alert' + 'High Alert' (excluding Very High Alert), the only row affected is Somalia (111.3), which would drop from the CSV.
decision_log: 1) Seed provenance: question staged from `datasets/pkdb_bench/docs/example_questions.txt` entry #10 ('Which countries are considered to have become politically unstable in each continent after 2000?'). The protocol §4 mentions an FSI-anchored example for `causal` with similar phrasing. **Cycle-1 BLOCKING fix**: title softened from 'become politically unstable since 2000' to 'currently classified as politically fragile or unstable' because FSI is a current-year snapshot, not a temporal 'since 2000' measure. The auditor flagged the overclaim explicitly: 'The cited FSI source supports a 2024 fragility snapshot and even says FSI indicators are a snapshot in time; it does not establish that each listed country became unstable after 2000.' The new title matches the FSI snapshot reality. 2) Chose query_category=causal because 'politically fragile or unstable' is a derived/inferred state (FSI is a composite of 12 indicators capturing political/economic/security causes). The protocol §4 example explicitly maps this kind of query to causal. 3) **Cycle-1 BLOCKING fix**: source-tier framing declared as honest Tier B (manual_wikipedia) rather than Tier C. The cited URLs are all Wikipedia; the underlying primary source is Fund for Peace, but this instance uses Wikipedia's mirror. Per the auditor: 'Either make it honestly Tier B/manual Wikipedia, or switch to the Fund for Peace FSI source.' Going with the former — Tier B honestly. The protocol §4 lists FSI as a Tier C example, but the data is also defensibly accessible via Wikipedia (Tier B), and the rows are the same. 4) **Cycle-2 BLOCKING fix (project-level)**: operation_type back to 'filter' per the cycle-2 audit's preferred path. The cycle-1 'projection' choice was UI-compliant but semantically false (db_analog has `WHERE fsi_score_2024 >= 90` — structurally a filter). The fix is at the project level: `curation_ui/app.py` validator now allows causal → {projection, aggregation, filter} (was {projection, aggregation}); `references/workflows.md` preflight #4 documents the new pairing. The instance now correctly declares its filter operation without the validator warning. 5) Inclusion criterion: FSI 2024 score ≥ 90 (i.e., country is in Alert, High Alert, or Very High Alert sub-tier). Including all three sub-tiers; the protocol's 'Alert and High Alert' phrasing is interpreted to mean the full Alert category (≥90 threshold), since excluding Very High Alert (the MOST unstable tier) would make no sense for an 'unstable countries' query. 6) Used FSI 2024 (most recent year on Wikipedia) rather than FSI 2023. Risk: 2024 may be near or past LLM pretraining cutoffs; the LLM may have stronger recall of FSI 2022/2023. Documented in temporal_note. 7) Country names follow country_converter v1.3.2 short_name canonical forms. Two normalizations applied vs. Wikipedia's FSI list naming: 'Congo-Kinshasa' → 'DR Congo' (cc canonical); 'Congo-Brazzaville' / 'Republic of the Congo' → 'Congo Republic' (cc short_name). cc spot check: 0 mismatches after normalization. 8) Continent assignments follow Wikipedia 'List of sovereign states and dependent territories by continent' (UN M49-aligned). Yemen and Lebanon are Asia per UN M49. Egypt would be Africa per UN M49 (but Egypt's FSI 2024 score is 88.2, below the 90 threshold, so it is not in this CSV). 9) South America, Oceania, and Antarctica have zero rows because no countries on those continents have FSI 2024 ≥ 90. Documenting that as 'sparse coverage' rather than 'data missing' — the absence is the source-defined answer. 10) PK on (Continent, Country) — composite PK because the continent partition is a load-bearing dimension of the seed question.
normalization_decisions: Continent values use the standard 7-continent English names per the Wikipedia continent assignment article; 4 of 7 appear in the CSV (Africa, Asia, Europe, North America). Country names follow country_converter v1.3.2 short_name canonical forms; specifically 'DR Congo' for Democratic Republic of the Congo and 'Congo Republic' for the Republic of the Congo (not the unabbreviated forms). 'Palestine' is treated as a country (UN observer state). FSI Tier values use the Wikipedia FSI nomenclature exactly — 'Alert', 'High Alert', 'Very High Alert' (note: the article also has 'Warning' / 'Stable' / 'Sustainable' tiers, all excluded here). FSI Score values are the FSI 2024 numeric scores from Wikipedia, kept to one decimal place where the source provides that precision. Sort order is (Continent ASC, Country ASC).
open_questions: 1) FSI 2024 was published mid-2024 and may be near or past some LLMs' pretraining cutoffs. The LLM under test may have stronger recall of FSI 2022 or 2023 rankings than 2024. 2) The protocol §4 Tier C example for `causal` says 'Alert and High Alert' tiers — two-tier naming — but the modern FSI uses three sub-tiers within the Alert category. This instance includes all three (≥90 threshold) on the principled basis that excluding the MOST unstable tier (Very High Alert) makes no sense for an 'unstable countries' query. If a future curator prefers strict 'Alert' + 'High Alert' only, Somalia (the only Very High Alert country) would drop. 3) Source tier is honestly Tier B (Wikipedia) rather than Tier C (Fund for Peace primary). The data is identical; the framing is the question. A future curator could switch to Tier C by adding Fund for Peace URL and using gt_construction='web_search_fragile_states_index'; this instance commits to Tier B Wikipedia per the audit's recommended path. 4) operation_type='projection' is a UI-compliance choice; the instance is structurally a filter (FSI score ≥ 90). The semantic mismatch is documented; if the UI validator's category-pairings are updated to allow causal → filter in the future, operation_type could be changed back. 5) Continent assignments follow UN M49 (per Wikipedia). 'Middle East' as a region is split between Asia (most rows) and Africa (no rows here since Egypt is below the 90 threshold in 2024). 6) FSI is one of several political-stability/fragility indices (others: World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators, Economist Intelligence Unit Democracy Index, Freedom House Freedom in the World). Each gives a different 'unstable countries' list. The instance commits to FSI as the source-grounded anchor; alternative anchors yield different sets. 7) South America (0 rows) is notable — Venezuela was previously in the High Alert tier but recent FSI rankings have moved it just below 90 (88.2 in 2024). The empty South-America partition is faithful to the FSI 2024 anchor. 8) Country name normalization: cc spot check confirmed 0 mismatches after applying 'DR Congo' and 'Congo Republic' canonical forms; all other 27 distinct country tokens are already cc canonical.
